comment: Sound catalogue of the radar. firmware/dragonradar/sounds.h is generated from this by the common tools/gen_sounds.mjs (each entry: name, tempo, notes in the melody format of sound.h: raw HZ:MS tones and R:MS rests, ~square / ~sine / ~tri switches the waveform of the tones that follow). gain (0-100, percent of the user volume) and the beep block are read by tools/gen_radar.mjs (radar_assets.h), the preview and tools/preview/render_wav.mjs; the other fields are documentation. Matched to a measured clip of the anime's radar (pitch, harmonics and timing only; the clip is not in the repo): each beep is a 'pi-PI', about 80 ms at 2130 Hz then 60 ms an octave up at 4260 Hz, close to a triangle wave (3rd harmonic about 0.13); power on opens with a 2100 +- 100 Hz warble. See docs/design.md.

synth.comment: How every renderer plays a tone (matches the ES8311 synth of sound.cpp): square (naive), sine, or a band-limited triangle (its odd harmonics up to 0.45 x sampleRate, amplitude 1/k^2), at sampleRate. Amplitude ramps over rampMs at each change. Level of full scale at user volume v (0-100, after the effect's gain: v = volume x gain / 100): levelAt100 x 10^(-rangeDb x (1 - v/100)^curveShape / 20), and 0 at v = 0; with these values volume 60 is -3.6 dB, 30 is -16 dB and 10 is -28 dB. Raw HZ:MS tones are legato (no gap between them).

beep.comment: The radar beep repeats while at least one ball is known. Its interval depends on the distance d (metres) of the nearest ball, on a log scale: t = clamp((log10(farM) - log10(d)) / (log10(farM) - log10(nearM)), 0, 1); interval = maxIntervalMs + (minIntervalMs - maxIntervalMs) x t^curvePow. The distance is absolute, so zooming does not change the rhythm. The dots flash on every beep (radar.json blink). Crossing closeM plays ball_close once and crossing foundM plays ball_found once; each re-arms when the distance grows past threshold x rearmFactor.

sfx.name: power_on
sfx.es: Encendido: tono que tiembla mientras se enciende la pantalla y dos "pi-PI" con el marcador y la onda
sfx.en: Power on: a warbling tone while the screen lights up and two "pi-PI" with the marker and the scan ring

sfx.name: radar_beep
sfx.es: El "pi-PI" del radar: dos tonos a una octava; se repite más rápido cuanto más cerca está la esfera
sfx.en: The radar "pi-PI": two tones an octave apart; repeats faster the closer the nearest ball is

sfx.name: zoom_out
sfx.es: Botón de arriba: el "brrr" del botón y un blip agudo al alejar la escala
sfx.en: Top button: the button "brrr" and a high blip when zooming out

sfx.name: button
sfx.es: Pulsar un botón o la pantalla: el "brrr" que tiembla entre 2000 y 2200 Hz del clip del anime, antes del pitido
sfx.en: Any button or screen press: the "brrr" warbling between 2000 and 2200 Hz in the anime clip, before the beep

sfx.name: zoom_in
sfx.es: Acercar la escala: el mismo "brrr" con un blip más grave
sfx.en: Zoom in: the same "brrr" with a lower blip

sfx.name: ball_close
sfx.es: Una esfera entra a menos de 30 m: tres "pi-PI" rápidos
sfx.en: A ball comes within 30 m: three quick "pi-PI"

sfx.name: ball_found
sfx.es: Esfera encontrada (a menos de 3 m): cuatro notas que suben y un pip final
sfx.en: Ball found (within 3 m): four rising notes and a final pip

sfx.name: power_off
sfx.es: Apagado: barrido que baja mientras se apaga la pantalla
sfx.en: Power off: a falling sweep while the screen goes dark
